| [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) v9 | Transient support can be withdrawn safely only if it started a process that keeps itself going on a flux that will stay available, was large enough to carry the supported party past any threshold that process has, outlasted the threat it stood in for, and left the work to the party throughout, in each subtask it must later do alone and not only in its role as a whole, at no more effort than it could bear, and, where the capacity is cumulative and its field moves fast, kept up after withdrawal; inputs the party cannot produce must stay supplied as a standing part of the arrangement; support that fails these leaves dependence or decay, but meeting them all is not enough, since support can carry a function nobody names before withdrawal; and persistence after withdrawal is needed to tell which, though slow reversion can mimic it | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to characterize "what differentiates transient support that induces dependency and is hazardous to remove from transient support that builds new capabilities and is safe to remove", with reintroduction and ecological recovery proposed as cases. It draws together the branch's three domains: DNA origami, aid and development, and ecology. Three conditions are needed for it. First, the support starts a self-sustaining process on an ambient flux instead of doing the upkeep. Planted tree islands, weeded for 2.5 years, kept their advantage to 16–18 years because established trees keep drawing seed dispersers (Holl et al.; Schubert et al.). Supplied repair, by contrast, never becomes optional ([CLAIM-597](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-597.md)). Second, the threat it stood in for is gone. Conservation-reliant species stay reliant while fire is suppressed or habitat threats persist (Mussmann et al.; Brown et al.). Third, the party did the work throughout. Support that does the work wears capacity down by disuse ([CLAIM-558](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-558.md)), by slack effort (Ostrom et al.) or by selection for the supported conditions, which costs hatchery steelhead fitness in the wild within one generation (Christie et al.). Captive-bred translocated stock shows negative population growth (Morris et al.). Persistence must be shown after withdrawal: impact at exit and judged success both overstate it. Revised the same day after two counterpoints the owner asked for. Evidence against the lazy-poor stereotype finds no slack effort in poor households: cash transfers barely change work, and one-off graduation packages raise it. So that route is confined to help that is assured and permanent. A household asset threshold (Balboni et al.) adds a condition on size: support too small decays with no dependence at all. Urban development adds three cautions. Some public inputs are a standing part of a coproduced service (Evans; Watson). Forty years of persistence can be slow reversion (Kline and Moretti). And a place can last while the people it served are dispersed (Collins and Shester; LaVoice). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. Moved into the SYNTHESIS scheme on 2026-11-07 ([ADR-077](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-077.md)) and returned to CLAIM on 2026-11-08 (ADR-084), keeping the standing the status review of 2026-11-06 gave it under the rulings the owner delegated. | Active |
| [CLAIM-603](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) v6 | A capability lost because another reliably supplies it is the Black Queen's loss, favoured to the one who loses it, and whether it is dependency or division of labour is decided by the supply, not the loss: one-way supply set from outside, as aid is, leaves a dependence that nothing in the dependent's dynamics limits and that withdrawal punishes, while reciprocal loss, each partner supplying what the other gave up, leaves interdependence, so the aim framed as self-sufficiency is better framed as reciprocity | The assistant's, on the owner's remark of 2026-11-05 that "assured help makes recipients lose skill" sounds "closely related to niche differentiation and specialization phenomena". The record holds the biology. On the Black Queen Hypothesis ([THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)) a cell that stops making a leaky public good saves its cost while others still supply it, so the loss is favoured to the individual and spreads. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. The Samaritan's dilemma has the same logic (Ostrom et al.), and Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's recipient is better off in the high-aid state. The loss itself is not the pathology. What differs is the supply. A Black Queen loss stops by itself when helpers grow rare, because the helpers are the same population. Aid is set from outside and does not fall as dependence grows, so nothing stops the loss short of what aid covers, and withdrawal returns the cost ([CLAIM-602](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-602.md)). Buchnera's loss runs both ways, and the result is interdependence. A state that taxes its citizens (Moore) is in the same position: it lost nothing, it exchanges. After the owner linked the claim to the gift economy of Burning Man, readings of Mauss, of St John on Burning Man and of Heins, Unrau and Avram added two things. One-way supply costs the receiver standing as well as capacity: in Mauss the unreturned gift makes its receiver inferior. And the return need not go back to the giver: it can travel round a circuit, as Mauss's do, or out to a whole community, as Burning Man's is meant to, and both sit beside a demand for self-reliance. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CLAIM-886](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-886.md) | Symmetric competition with bounded niche adaptation does not secure recovery against residents that re-adapt: in a two-resource trade-off, a stable pair of specialists, each recovering when rare against a frozen partner, coexists with a stable lone generalist against which a removed specialist has negative growth, and a lone specialist leaves its corner for the vacated niche when c/B < a'(0)/a'(1) | The counterexample [LEAD-049](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-049.md) asked for, within [CLAIM-885](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-885.md)'s class. Two resources with supply (B, B) and cost c. u(θ) = (a(θ), a(1 − θ)), θ in [0, 1], with a(0) = 0 and a(1) = 1. The specialists at θ = 1 and θ = 0, each with abundance B − c, are locally exponentially stable when B > c > 0 and a'(1) > a'(0). Each recovers at B − c against its frozen partner. But a lone specialist's margin at its corner is a'(1)c − a'(0)B. So when c/B < a'(0)/a'(1) it moves into the vacated resource. Against the symmetric lone generalist, a specialist's growth is c(1/(2a(1/2)) − 1). That is negative when a(1/2) > 1/2, when the generalist's total uptake beats a specialist's. For a(t) = t − ½t²(1 − t) + 3t²(1 − t)², with a'(0) = 1, a'(1) = 3/2 and a(1/2) = 5/8, the lone generalist is itself a stable state, and the removed specialist's growth there is −c/5. | [CLAIM-919](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-919.md) | In a population of adaptive operators whose training follows influence, whether a rare-context specialist that loses its influence regains it is decided by whether spare capacity can take its niche in the meantime, not by whether it keeps its competence: with spare operators its niche is refilled and it stays shut out even with its competence intact, and without them nothing refills its niche and it returns even with its competence mostly lost | [QUESTION-134](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-134.md) asks whether influence-dependent training makes a marginalized specialist lose its competence, so that it cannot regain influence when its contexts recur. The rare specialist's share was clamped at 10⁻³ for 20,000 steps and then released, under four influence rules and 6 seeds. With two spare operators, a spare took the niche and became as competent as the specialist. The specialist failed to return in 23 of 24 rule-seed pairs per arm, whether its training had been decoupled from its influence (competence kept) or coupled with a maintenance cost (competence mostly lost). It lost its competence afterwards, once coupled again. With no spare operator, nothing refilled the niche, and the specialist returned every time, even frozen with most of its competence gone. Loss of access cost competence only where maintenance had a cost. Loss of influence came from pre-emption, and loss of competence followed it.
